newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metals futures mostly easier.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metals futures mostly easier.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures except silver ended mostly weaker on Tuesday, pressured by sporadic profit-taking, reflecting the yen's firmer tone against the dollar, traders said.
Silver futures were mostly firmer, backed by recent strength in spot silver prices, they said.
The August spot gold contract expired at noon at 1,345 yen per gran, down 3.0 yen with 2,349 lots of deliveries.
Other gold futures ranged from eight yen lower to one yen firmer. Benchmark June finished two yen down at 1,339 yen.
Spot gold was quoted at $389.20/389.50 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $389.20/389.70 in New York on Monday.

Activity in the spot gold market was quiet. "Spot gold prices were steady during the Asian hours amid a lack of selling. Gold could test $390 in overseas markets later today," a senior dealer of a foreign bank said.

The spot platinum August contract expired at noon, down six yen with 436 lots of deliveries. Other prices ranged from unchanged to five yen per gram lower with benchmark June ending down five at 1,374 yen.

Traders here said Russian platinum shipments to Japan for August delivery have been delayed by up to three weeks, but investors were not rush to buy platinum as the Japanese platinum market is currently balanced.

The spot August silver contract expired at 183.4 yen, down 0.8 yen per 10 grams with 274 lots of deliveries. Other prices ranged from unchanged to 0.7 yen per 10 grams higher. Benchmark June ended up 0.5 yen at 184.3 yen. The spot August palladium contract expired at 422 yen, down six yen with 456 lots of deliveries. Benchmark June ended down two at 437 yen.
